subject: Re: Alignment required: ClearWay conditional feature gating & contract milestone
messages:
From: Emily Park <emily@clearway.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft SOW + conditional feature ask for RFP milestone

Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — team was impressed with the latency and routing controls. Procurement surfaced a hard milestone in our RFP: we need a tenant-level redaction hook and a deterministic export flag in the inference pipeline by the contract effective date (Sept 15) for our internal audit.

We realize that is a product ask, so we're trying to see what a conditional commitment looks like from Redwood: would you (or someone on product) be willing to sign an SOW with a milestone that is contingent on a small scope change? Our legal team prefers the ask be captured as a deliverable with acceptance criteria.

I've attached the draft SOW we will send to procurement. If you can map engineering effort (rough T-shirt) and an ETA window, that would help speed approvals on our side. Happy to do a quick call Monday.

Cheers,
Emily Park
Head of Cloud Procurement | ClearWay Finance
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Park <emily@clearway.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Aug 2028 18:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Draft SOW + conditional feature ask for RFP milestone

Emily —

Appreciate the clarity and the SOW. Looping in Marissa (Product) and Ben (Eng) so we can translate the acceptance criteria into scope and ETA.

High level: the two asks (tenant redaction hook + deterministic export flag) look scoped but not huge — depends on whether deterministic export needs a new export pipeline or can be a toggle in the existing KV snapshot flow.

Marissa / Ben — would you be able to review the attached SOW and propose a minimal acceptance test and a range for delivery (best-case / conservative)? If we can give ClearWay a defendable milestone window, I can push for inclusion in the SOW as a conditional deliverable and lock the deal.

Emily — can you confirm whether ClearWay needs FIPS/KMS integration in this milestone or if that's out of scope (we heard that may be later)?

Jonas
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Aug 2028 13:40:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Draft SOW + conditional feature ask for RFP milestone

Jonas / Ben —

I reviewed ClearWay_SOW_v3.pdf and sketched a minimal acceptance criteria in the attached redwood-proposal-feature-diff.md. Key notes:

- Tenant redaction hook: implement as an outbound post-processor callback that receives tokenized output + metadata; acceptance is a test harness where a set of PII-laced prompts are redacted to the provided policy within 3ms additional latency (per request).

- Deterministic export flag: best-case we expose a flag that forces canonical ordering for export snapshots and includes run_id hashing to ensure bit-for-bit reproducibility for a fixed model + prompt seed. Conservative path requires a small export runner (2 person-weeks + QA).

Estimated effort (conservative): 3 sprints (2 engineers) for both items including tests and minor infra changes; best-case we can do a trimmed timeline in 4 weeks if we prioritize and accept a canary-only rollout.

Constraints / ask from legal: we need a simple acceptance test (sample inputs + expected sanitized outputs) and a staging environment with access for ClearWay audit.

Ben — can you confirm infra risk and whether we need a temporary residency slot for the canary?

Marissa Cole
VP, Product Management | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Aug 2028 09:58:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Draft SOW + conditional feature ask for RFP milestone

Marissa — thanks for the breakdown. Quick engineering read:

- Redaction hook: straightforward; we already have outbound transformers that can be extended. Add ~0.5 engineer-month + test harness + a short perf regression sweep.

- Deterministic export: trickier because of current async snapshot ordering. Conservative cost: 2 engineer-months to implement a deterministic exporter with a reproducibility hash and test suite. If we take the canary-only route and narrow acceptance (sampling vs full dataset), we can cut that to ~3 engineer-weeks.

Infra ask: would like a canary residency slot and temp access to ClearWay staging (IP allowlist) to validate exports end-to-end. That will avoid surprises during acceptance.

I think Marissa's 3-sprint conservative estimate aligns with our numbers if we ship both features with proper QA.

Ben Carter
Director, Inference Platform | Redwood Inference
From: Emily Park <emily@clearway.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: ClearWay Procurement <procurement@clearway.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Aug 2028 21:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft SOW + conditional feature ask for RFP milestone

Team —

This is helpful, thank you. Procurement will accept a conditional deliverable with the conservative timeline (target acceptance window Sept 10–20) provided Redwood: 1) defines the acceptance test (we'll sign), 2) gives staging access for verification, and 3) confirms that the deliverable will be feature-gated so we can opt into the canary.

I'll push the SOW through procurement with those items and ping once I have a legal sign-off. If Redwood can provide the acceptance test template today, we can attach it to the SOW and shorten legal review.

Emily Park
Head of Cloud Procurement | ClearWay Finance
